title: Reduce presubmit noise by consolidating bootstrapping and splitting the toolchain loader
author: Tariq Patel
description: Context: our presubmit lanes have grown noisy and slow due to duplicated bootstrapping steps across language workspaces and an eager toolchain installer that runs unconditionally. Motivation: shrink presubmit latency, reduce CI flakes from network installs, and make local dev iteration closer to CI by centralizing toolchain initialization and making installs conditional. What I changed: 1) Introduced a single lightweight toolchain loader (tools/ci/toolchain-loader.go) that queries a per-repo manifest and performs idempotent installs; 2) Split heavy download/install steps into an opt-in stage invoked only when toolchain fingerprints change; 3) Reworked GitHub presubmit composite action to call the loader with a fast-path check that skips installs on cache hits; 4) Moved language-specific bootstraps into scripts/toolchain-profiles/ and added small shim scripts for local dev; 5) Updated lint/test pipelines to prefer cached artifacts and to fail fast for obvious compilation errors before running expensive integration suites; 6) Added telemetry counters and a short-lived feature flag to enable staged rollout. Testing: local `./scripts/ci/smoke-presubmit.sh` across go/python/ts, CI runs on branch: unit+lint (fast) -> toolchain-check (fast fingerprint) -> conditional install -> integration. Rollout plan: rollout 50% of PR traffic for two days, monitor presubmit latency and cache-hit rates, then enable globally and remove the flag. Checklist: [x] unit tests for loader logic [x] integration smoke on staging CI [x] documented migration notes in tools/ci/README [x] small README for local dev shims [x] linear tickets linked Impact: expected median presubmit time reduction ~30-45% for typical commits, decrease in external network flakiness, simpler dev onboarding. Notes: this refactors bootstrapping but does not change artifact signing or release automation steps; follow-up PR will unify release preflight hooks to use the same loader.
